title_original: AFM takeaways: hot packages and Summit recap - The Screen Podcast
excerpt_original: Americas editor Jeremy Kay and Europe editor Tim Dams report from Los Angeles.

blocks.text: On this week’s episode of The Screen Podcast, the team unpacks the American Film Market (AFM), including the hot packages and takeaways from the AFM summit.
Americas editor Jeremy Kay and Europe editor Tim Dams said the talk of the summit was the proposed federal production incentive and the new era of content creators.

“There’s this sense of a gold rush and everybody’s wanting to find the next Curry Barker or Kane Parsons, but beware. There’s no guarantee that there’s going to be an Obsession or a Backrooms every year in a summer,” Kay said.

”But certainly people are out there now trying to find those new talents and the studios are looking for that kind of thing as well and a way of really connecting with these exciting young filmmakers who have these inbuilt audiences.”

Then Kay is joined by Arnaud Rolland, CNC’s deputy head of digital, and Daphne Lora, head of Film France-CNC and Game France-CNC, to discuss the updates to France’s Tax Rebate For International Productions (TRIP).
To download or subscribe to future episodes, search for ‘The Screen Podcast’, which is available on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , Acast and YouTube .

This week’s episode was sponsored by Film France-CNC. The CNC showcase, titled US filmmaking in France: Living the French Experience, took place in Los Angeles last week and included an update on how US film and TV productions can access France’s filming incentive, the Tax Rebate For International Productions (TRIP).
The Screen Podcast is produced by Ellie Calnan, with Wendy Mitchell serving as editorial director. New episodes every Thursday.
